transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-07-21
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 42 minutes (approx)
Attendees: Jordan Myers (Redwood AE), Priya Desai (Redwood SE), Liam O'Connor (Product), Aisha Khan (SummitHealth Platform), Mark Rivera (SummitHealth SRE), Dana Liu (SummitHealth Head of ML), Evan Torres (SummitHealth Security)

Auto-generated summary (may be rough):
- Redwood walked SummitHealth through the Console tracing, request logs, and error analysis flows.
- Demo focused on tracing a failing streaming request, how to correlate request-ids to logs and traces, and recommended debugging playbook.
- Discussed integration points for VPC/private deployments, KMS encryption, and pilot scope (100 req smoke test).

Topics:
- Request IDs and tracing correlation
- Error analysis and root-cause workflow
- Console filters and saved queries
- Exporting traces and sharing with Redwood SE for deeper analysis
- How Optimize suggestions surface batching/quantization tradeoffs for cost vs latency

Transcript:
00:00 Jordan Myers: hey folks uh welcome thanks for joining, um we'll give a quick 20-25 minute walkthrough of the console tracing and then leave time for questions. is that still the plan on your side?
00:07 Aisha Khan: yep that's the plan, thanks Jordan. We wanted to see the end-to-end debug flow, like if a streaming response truncates or errors, how do we find root cause.
00:15 Jordan Myers: great, Priya will lead the demo and Liam will chime on product-level recommendations.
00:21 Priya Desai: thanks, okay I'm sharing screen now — um, tell me if you can't see the console.
00:29 Mark Rivera: seeing it. The top nav shows tracing, requests, models, etc.
00:34 Priya Desai: exactly. So first thing — every request returns a request-id header which is the key to link logs, traces, and the KV cache evidence. here i pasted a failing request-id so we'll search it. note: the console captures both hosted and dedicated request flows if you have private routing enabled.
00:50 Dana Liu: when you say KV cache evidence do you mean the key-value cache on the inference runtime? sometimes docs say KV cash — we've seen the typo in other exports.
00:56 Priya Desai: yes KV cache — apologies, typos in the transcript engines. in the console you can view the cache hit rate per request.
01:05 Priya Desai: (click) so here's the request view. top shows metadata, latency breakdown, tokens billed, and a timeline with steps: route, queue wait, model compile, generation.
01:20 Priya Desai: if we scroll to the right there's a trace waterfall — each segment is instrumented: network -> routing -> runtime -> model.
01:29 Evan Torres: are those spans correlated with our OpenTelemetry pipeline or is it Redwood-managed tracing?
01:34 Priya Desai: good question — right now they are Redwood-managed spans, but we provide an export that maps to OTEL format so you can ingest into your tracing backend. that'll include trace-id and parent spans.
01:44 Mark Rivera: perfect, so we can join on trace-id in our own Jaeger/Tempo.
01:48 Jordan Myers: yes exactly. we usually send a small json export attached to the support ticket to help debug.
01:53 Aisha Khan: show us an error scenario please, how do we get from a user-facing error to root cause?
01:58 Priya Desai: sure. here's a streaming request that returned an early termination error — the console highlights the error step in red.
02:05 Priya Desai: (scroll) the error panel gives the runtime error code, message, and if available the stack snippet from our runtime (this is obfuscated for hosted customers but full detail is available for dedicated pilots).
02:17 Dana Liu: obfuscated — do you mean pii is removed or you mean internal runtime symbols?
02:22 Priya Desai: internal runtime symbols are obfuscated for hosted, yes. for dedicated or private deployments with a support NDA we can provide more detailed stack frames.
02:31 Jordan Myers: also for compliance folks — we redact user prompt content from aggregate logs unless you opt in.
02:38 Evan Torres: how does that interact with our retention policy? we keep logs for 90 days in prod, and any export needs to be encrypted with our KMS.
02:46 Priya Desai: console supports per-route retention windows and KMS-wrapped exports. you can configure RBAC to limit who can export traces.
02:54 Mark Rivera: demo the saved query filters — we often need to baseline slow requests and save that filter.
02:59 Priya Desai: good call, yes. (types) here i create a filter: latency > 1500ms AND model: redwood-700b-quant. save it, name it "High-latency 7/21" and now it appears in the left nav. saved queries can be shared as links.
03:20 Aisha Khan: can we trigger alerts on saved queries? like an opt-in alert to slack?
03:24 Priya Desai: currently we support webhook alerts and email; Slack integration is coming next quarter but you can route webhook to a lambda to forward to Slack.
03:33 Liam O'Connor: from a product perspective our Optimize module will also surface a suggested batching config if we detect consistent patterns of short requests — that lives on the same spot as the request view.
03:42 Dana Liu: will Optimize recommend quantization changes per-model automatically or is that a manual recommendation?
03:47 Liam O'Connor: it proposes profiles with expected latency/cost deltas and a confidence score. you can preview a simulated cost change before applying.
03:55 Mark Rivera: back to the error trace — how do we collect the full network trace? sometimes we see a 502 from an upstream and need the full TCP timing.
04:03 Priya Desai: console attaches the gateway timing and your backend response timing if you use our route backends; for external upstreams we surface the outbound timing and headers but we don't proxy the full TCPk dump. for that level you would pull your VPC logs.
04:16 Aisha Khan: ok understood. show us how we'd hand this off to Redwood support if we can't resolve.
04:22 Priya Desai: click "Share with Redwood" on the request — you select the level of detail, attach the saved query, and include notes. that creates a support bundle with traces and a link to the request ids.
04:33 Jordan Myers: that's what we use to speed up root cause — the bundle includes the OTEL export plus our runtime metrics.
04:40 Dana Liu: what about GDPR or PII concerns if we share a support bundle?
04:44 Priya Desai: you choose redact options at share time: remove prompt/response content, strip user ids, or include full data if you have data-sharing agreement.
04:53 Evan Torres: our security process needs SAML/SSO integration and RBAC mapping to AD groups; can the console integrate with our IdP?
04:59 Jordan Myers: yes we support SAML2 SSO and SCIM provisioning. RBAC can be mapped to groups and you can restrict export permissions.
05:07 Mark Rivera: let's try a troubleshooting workflow — we have a manifest of 5 failing request IDs from a weekend run. what's the step-by-step inside Redwood?
05:15 Priya Desai: ideal flow: customer runs smoke test -> collect request-ids -> filter in console -> confirm error type (runtime vs model vs network) -> if runtime or model, share bundle with Redwood -> we triage and provide a root cause and remediation (hotfix or config).
05:29 Priya Desai: i'm going to paste one of your request IDs (fake for demo) and step through the waterfall.
05:35 (typing)
05:42 Priya Desai: okay this one shows a long compile step — the model compile took 800ms due to cold-start on a quantized variant. the generation was fine but the latency spike was the compile.
05:52 Dana Liu: compile? is that the kernel selection you mentioned in docs?
05:56 Priya Desai: yes — kernel selection and some graph rewrites happen if the sequence length isn't in profile; we cache compiled kernels but cold starts can occur if the instance scaled up.
06:05 Mark Rivera: do you surface the cache hit ratio per instance? we need to tie it to autoscale events.
06:10 Priya Desai: you can correlate with infra metrics; the trace has a tag for instance id and an autoscale event is visible in the timeline.
06:17 Jordan Myers: quick note — for Dedicated customers you can pin prewarmed instances to avoid compile cold starts. that's usually in the pilot discussion.
06:24 Aisha Khan: good to know. what about function/tool calling faults — if a tool call returns 500 mid-stream, how is that shown?
06:31 Priya Desai: it surfaces as a child span with the tool payload and response headers. you can replay that tool call from the console if the backend is captured or attach a sanitized payload.
06:41 Dana Liu: replay? so we can re-run the same request to reproduce?
06:45 Priya Desai: yes, replay from the console in a safe mode; it strips auth headers by default. for dedicated you can enable a more faithful replay.
06:53 Mark Rivera: there's chatter about token-level cost — can we see token-by-token cost breakdown for a request?
06:58 Priya Desai: the request view shows token counts and a cost estimate per token tier. it's approximate for hosted but exact in Dedicated with your pricing sheet.
07:07 Jordan Myers: time check — we're about 7 minutes in; we'll speed through a few saved queries and then show the export feature.
07:12 Priya Desai: (click) saved queries list — you can schedule exports of saved queries to S3. we support KMS encryption and prefixing by customer-id.
07:21 Aisha Khan: sending to S3 is important for compliance, yes. can it land in our own bucket under our account?
07:25 Priya Desai: yes, cross-account delivery into your bucket with role-assume is supported for Dedicated and Private deployments.
07:33 Evan Torres: sweet. next, SLA / alerting - can we tag a route as mission critical and get stricter SLOs?
07:40 Liam O'Connor: you can set route-level SLOs and link them to alerts; Dedicated customers can get higher uptime SLAs in the contract.
07:47 Aisha Khan: let's talk pilot scope quickly: we want a 2-week pilot, 1000 requests/day about a mix of streaming and short-turn queries, measure latency tail and cost. what's realistic?
07:58 Jordan Myers: that's doable — typical pilot is 2-4 weeks with an AE+SE support channel, and we recommend running with a prewarmed Dedicated pool for fair latency baselines.
08:07 Dana Liu: can we instrument our evaluation harness to emit a custom header so you can filter our synthetic load from real traffic?
08:12 Priya Desai: yes include x-summit-test: true and we can filter it via saved queries. we also recommend using a separate API key or route for pilot.
08:20 Mark Rivera: any limitations on the console UI when volume is high? sometimes we have millions of requests and UI slows down.
08:26 Priya Desai: saved queries and time-window paging avoid loading millions of rows; for large-volume analytics we recommend exporting to S3 and running OLAP queries.
08:33 Evan Torres: what about data residency? some EU data needs to stay in eu-west-1.
08:38 Jordan Myers: you can pin routes to regions; console respects region residency and we can configure retention per-region.
08:44 Aisha Khan: ok show the OTEL export real quick.
08:47 Priya Desai: (click) export bundle -> choose OTEL -> format: JSON -> include spans+metadata -> include or redact payload -> click export. link generated.
08:58 Priya Desai: i'll simulate downloading it. (pause) in the support bundle there's a trace.json and runtime-metrics.csv plus a request-log slice.
09:10 Mark Rivera: good. any gotchas for bringing these into our SIEM?
09:14 Priya Desai: the bundle is flattened and timestamped; you may need to remap field names for your SIEM. we provide a sample ingest script.
09:22 Jordan Myers: another common ask — correlation between Console and Optimize warnings. Liam, want to show how an Optimize suggestion links to a request pattern?
09:30 Liam O'Connor: sure. (navigate) Optimize flagged a route with many sub-100ms requests and suggests batching threshold 8 and a prefetch window. clicking into that suggestion shows the sample requests and projected cost savings.
09:42 Dana Liu: can Optimize do A/B rollback if a quantized profile causes quality regressions?
09:46 Liam O'Connor: yes, rollout policies include canary, percent-based rollouts, and automatic rollback if quality metrics (we track eval sets) degrade beyond threshold.
09:56 Aisha Khan: needed. our compliance team will want a log of rollouts and which model version served each request.
10:03 Priya Desai: console keeps model version history per request and a rollout audit trail in the Console's audit log.
10:10 Evan Torres: about audit log integrity — can we export logs to our SIEM with signed hashes?
10:15 Jordan Myers: we support append-only signed export packages for Dedicated customers; for Hosted we'd discuss enterprise retention add-on.
10:24 Mark Rivera: any examples of debugging a model regression? say quality dropped after a model swap.
10:29 Priya Desai: you'll use saved eval prompt set; console ties eval scores to model versions. we can diff embeddings or outputs and highlight prompts with largest regressions.
10:38 Dana Liu: and action item from that would be rollback or parameter tweak?
10:41 Liam O'Connor: either rollback via rollout policy or adjust temperature/top-p and re-run eval.
10:47 Aisha Khan: let's test the "Share with Redwood" flow — can you create a bundle without including full prompts so we can comply with privacy?
10:53 Priya Desai: selecting redact prompts will remove content and replace with hash placeholders; the trace structure still remains.
11:01 (brief crosstalk)
11:06 Jordan Myers: quick break in demo — we want to call out common pitfalls: mis-joined trace-ids (due to proxy rewriting headers), missing correlation ids in retry logic, and insufficient prewarm for quantized variants.
11:20 Mark Rivera: useful checklist. can you surface the autoscale events aligned to the tail latency spike?
11:26 Priya Desai: yes — timeline overlays autoscale and infra metrics so you can visually align spikes.
11:33 Aisha Khan: ok we're about halfway — can you show a real error bundle we can inspect?
11:38 Priya Desai: i pulled a recent one (sanitized). open it, top shows request metadata then the waterfall. the failure was an upstream 502 from a tool call which then surfaced as an aborted stream.
11:53 Dana Liu: so the root cause was the tool, not the model. how did Redwood present remediation?
11:58 Jordan Myers: for that case we suggested retry with backoff and a tool-side fix; we provided exact headers and payloads that triggered the failure.
12:06 Evan Torres: for ongoing monitoring do you provide runbooks or playbooks inside the Console?
12:10 Priya Desai: we attach recommended runbook steps to saved queries and support bundles — it's a checklist template you can customize.
12:18 Mark Rivera: great. last few questions: can we redact per-field (like user.email) when exporting?
12:24 Priya Desai: yes field-level redaction is supported via export policy. you can list JSON paths to redact.
12:30 Aisha Khan: one more on latency: you mentioned continuous batching — how do we see which requests were batched versus single-shot?
12:36 Liam O'Connor: trace spans include a batch_id tag when batched and batch size. you can filter on batch_id in saved queries.
12:44 Dana Liu: this was really helpful. any final notes on pricing for pilot?
12:48 Jordan Myers: we'll send a pilot pricing sheet — the main levers are whether you want prewarmed Dedicated capacity and whether you need cross-account S3 exports plus SOC2 add-on.
12:58 Aisha Khan: cool, we want to run the smoke test this week and share request-ids.
13:03 Jordan Myers: perfect. quick recap of next steps...
13:06 Jordan Myers: (recap) Priya will share the clip/screenshot and an example trace export; Jordan to send pilot SOW and pricing; Aisha to run smoke test and post request-ids; Evan to collate security Qs.
13:20 Aisha Khan: yes we'll do that. thanks all.
13:24 Jordan Myers: thanks everyone, we'll follow up in email with attachments.
13:28 (meeting ends)
